input: Laminate the kids' school emergency contact cards

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the cards need to be created from scratch or already exist determines how much work is involved before laminating can even begin.
The number of kids (and whether each child needs their own unique card) directly affects how many cards need to be made and laminated.
Whether the user owns a laminator, plans to buy one, or will use an outside service (e.g., office supply store) shapes the entire execution path.
A hard deadline (e.g., first day of school) changes prioritization and whether shortcuts like a print-and-laminate service are needed.
Whether the card is meant to be kept in a backpack, worn around the neck, or stored in a school file affects the required size and format.
Knowing what information must appear on the card (contacts, allergies, medical info, pickup authorization) determines the card's design and how much content to fit.
Understanding what 'done' looks like — e.g., one durable card per child handed to the teacher vs. a spare set at home — clarifies the final quantity and quality standard.

gold.taskTitle: Laminate kids' school emergency contact cards
gold.taskDescription: Prepare and laminate emergency contact cards for the children to use at school.

questions.title: Do the cards already exist, or do they need designing first?
questions.description: Determine whether the emergency contact cards are already printed and ready to laminate, or whether they still need to be created and printed.

questions.title: How many children need their own individual card?
questions.description: Establish the total number of cards needed, accounting for whether each child has a unique set of contacts or shares the same information.

questions.title: Do you have a laminator at home, or will you use a store?
questions.description: Identify the laminating method available — personal laminator, borrowed device, or a service at an office supply store — to plan the right steps.

questions.title: Is there a specific deadline these cards are needed by?
questions.description: Determine if there is a hard due date, such as the first day of school or an upcoming school event, that sets the pace for completing the task.

questions.title: Where will each card be kept — backpack, lanyard, or school file?
questions.description: Clarify the intended storage location for the laminated card, which determines the appropriate size, hole-punch needs, and thickness of laminate.

questions.title: What specific information must appear on each card?
questions.description: Identify all required content — emergency contacts, phone numbers, allergies, medical conditions, authorized pickup persons — to ensure nothing critical is left off.

questions.title: How many finished copies does each child need?
questions.description: Establish the target quantity per child — for example, one for the backpack, one for the teacher, and a spare at home — to define when the task is fully complete.
